title: The One-to-Many Relationship
summary: Explains how to model, implement, and query a one-to-many relationship while avoiding redundancy and preserving referential integrity.

concepts.title: One-to-many modeling
concepts.summary: A one-to-many relationship links one instance on one side to potentially many instances on the other and is shown with a crow's foot at the many end.

concepts.title: Separating repeated facts
concepts.summary: Moving facts that describe a separate entity into their own entity prevents the same fact from being repeated across many rows.

sections.title: Creating a database with a 1:m relationship

concepts.title: Foreign-key mapping
concepts.summary: A one-to-many relationship is implemented by placing the one-side identifier as a foreign key in the many-side table.

concepts.title: Referential integrity
concepts.summary: A non-null foreign-key value must match an existing referenced key so that relationships do not point to missing rows.

concepts.title: Two-table joins
concepts.summary: A join combines related rows by matching the foreign key in one table with the referenced key in the other.

concepts.title: Grouping related rows
concepts.summary: GROUP BY forms groups for aggregation, and HAVING filters the groups after aggregate values are computed.

concepts.title: Control-break reporting
concepts.summary: Grouped reports can calculate summaries for each value of a grouping attribute rather than for the table as a whole.

concepts.title: Subqueries and virtual tables
concepts.summary: Subqueries can isolate an intermediate result, while a view gives a saved query result a reusable virtual-table interface.
